item.description: Nina has your Friday Newsround. We have a special report about the rise in theft of Pokémon cards and De-Graft reports live from a school raising money for Children in Need.

item.title: Watch Newsround - signed and subtitled
item.description: A signed version of Newsround is available to watch every weekday for children who use British Sign Language.

item.title: Microsoft outage: How schools and gamers have been affected
item.description: A global Microsoft outage has been affecting services including Outlook, Teams and AI software Copilot leaving many people unable to send or receive messages. There have also been reports of problems with Xbox gaming caused by the outage. Find out more here.

item.title: What's happening for BBC Children in Need and are you doing anything to raise money?
item.description: Are you or your school putting on anything exciting to help raise money - maybe a bake sale, non uniform day, charity event or something super special?

item.title: KPop Demon Hunters Golden world tour announced
item.description: The tour website says Huntr/x "is ready to slay in a totally new way", with "live-action stunts and performers".

item.title: England beat France to win Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup
item.description: England have won the Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup for a record third time after beating France in a thrilling final in Australia. Find out more here.

item.title: Children in Need's Owain Wyn Evans raises £3.8m in epic bike ride
item.description: Radio 2 presenter Owain Wyn Evans has crossed the finish line after an epic five day cycle across the UK.

item.title: Why are shops locking away Pokémon cards and popular toys in cabinets?
item.description: Dozens of shops have moved popular products away from open shelves, as new figures reveal more than half a million recorded shoplifting offences.

item.title: Which toys would you pick for your favourite of all time list?
item.description: This year it's been decided that the game bingo, the cuddly toy Care Bears, The Pokémon Trading Card Game, and playground equipment the slide should get a spot in the National Toy Hall of Fame. Let us know in the comments which toys you would put in your top list.

item.title: Strange News: The weirdest stories of the week
item.description: What do dare devils, a robot and scientific art all have in common? They're all in this week's Strange of course! Emma-Louise has this one.

item.title: Quiz of the Week: Have you been following this week's news?
item.description: It's been a busy week of big stories and headlines. Have you been keeping up with the news over the last seven days? Test your knowledge of the latest top stories with our Quiz of the Week.

item.title: It's Friday 13th! But why is it believed to be unlucky?
item.description: Where did the fear of Friday 13th come from, why is it so famous and why do people think it's unlucky? Find out more here.

item.title: Harry Kane becomes England's most-capped male player
item.description: It was a special night for England captain Harry Kane as the Three Lions took on Croatia at Wembley Stadium. Find out more here.

item.title: What does kindness mean to you?
item.description: World Kindness Day celebrates being kind to yourself and others, but what does that look like to you?

item.title: Why is it suddenly so cold?
item.description: The outside temperature has suddenly dropped due to a blast of Arctic air moving down towards the UK. But what does a polar vortex have to do with this?

item.title: Manchester United sack manager Michael Carrick
item.description: The Red Devils manager has gone from signing two-year deal to being sacked 15 games later. Will Pochettino be taking his place?

item.title: Real Madrid star Vinícius Jr sends surprise message to boy in Sudan
item.description: Last year we met Zaher on Newsround to find out what life was like for him after he was injured in a drone strike. We now have a happy update and a surprise message from Real Madrid and Brazil footballer Vinícius Jr.

item.title: Should phones be allowed at the table in restaurants?
item.description: A group of restaurants in Italy will be banning phones at the table as part of a trial to get families talking more, do you think screen-free dining is a good idea? Have your say here...

item.title: Forming a band and growing crops: What a year in a simulated Mars mission is really like
item.description: Four people have spent a year seeing what it would be like to live on Mars...without leaving Earth.

item.title: Remembrance: What is it and why is it important?
item.description: Remembrance Day, or Armistice Day, commemorates the day World War One ended and is a time to remember all those who have died in wars. It's marked with a period of silence at the eleventh hour of the eleventh day of the eleventh month.

item.title: Remembrance Sunday in pictures
item.description: Remembrance Sunday is a day when people around the UK and across the world spend time remembering those who have given their lives serving in the armed forces.

item.title: How did World War One come to an end?
item.description: It started in 1914 and ended in 1918. It has been over 100 years since the end of the first war to truly affect the whole world - World War One.

item.title: VE Day: What is it, when is it and why do we remember?
item.description: VE Day - or Victory in Europe Day - marks the day when fighting against Nazi Germany in Europe came to an end on 8 May 1945.

item.title: VJ Day 2025: 'My great grandfather won the Victoria Cross'
item.description: This year is the 80th anniversary of Victory over Japan Day which marked the end of the Second World War. Millions of soldiers from all over the world, including 2.5 million from India, helped Britain and its Allies win the war.

item.title: How much do you know about Remembrance poppies?
item.description: In the weeks before Remembrance Sunday, you will see lots of people wearing and carrying poppies.

item.title: What is D-Day and why is it important?
item.description: The D-Day landings took place on 6 June 1944 during World War Two. The landings marked the start of the campaign to free north-west Europe from the Nazis. Find out more in our guide.

item.title: What's happening for BBC Children in Need and are you doing anything to raise money?
item.description: Are you or your school putting on anything exciting to help raise money - maybe a bake sale, non uniform day, charity event or something super special?

item.title: How strict is your school about phones?
item.description: Pupils in England will not be allowed to have their mobile phones with them at all during the school day, the government has announced. Find out more here.

item.title: Would you like to go into space?
item.description: Ever dreamed of flying to the Moon and helping to build a base there? Nasa has opened applications for explorers to help in their next chapter of human spaceflight, and there are a few things you'll need before you can make that dream come true.

item.title: Do you watch TV with the subtitles on?
item.description: A survey suggests that younger people are more used to watching shows with the subtitles, saying it helps them understand what was going on, concentrate better and avoid missing important plot lines. Do you put the subs when watching your favourite shows, and if so - why?

item.title: Which musical artist or band would you love to sing with?
item.description: With pupils from Sam Fender's old school singing on his brand new single for this year's John Lewis Christmas advert, we want to know which star you'd love to sing with.

item.title: How to get in touch with Newsround
item.description: Newsround wouldn't be the show all we know and love without you guys watching and getting involved - here's how you can contact us.

item.description: This week's Happy News De-Graft has a panda celebration, some beavers being released into the wild at Loch Ness and an Italian deli made entirely out of wool!

item.title: Your Planet: Environmental news from around the world
item.description: De-Graft has this week's Your Planet, with the cutest dormice, challenging conditions for Christmas trees, and a drone delivery for rescued chimps.

item.title: People across the UK and the world pay tribute on Armistice Day
item.description: At 11am on the 11th day of the 11th month, people commemorate the end of the First World War and remember those who have died in conflicts.

item.title: Why penguin poo can cause Antarctic ice to melt
item.description: Scientists have found that penguin poo, called guano, can cause Antarctic snow to melt at a faster than normal rate.

item.title: Rare Manx seabird returned in conservation mission
item.description: A group of 40 young Manx shearwater seabirds have been taken to the Isle of Canna to try and re-establish the population there.

item.title: Prize-winning kid photographers share their top tips for the perfect shot
item.description: Not one but two kids from the UK have bagged top prizes at one of the world's most famous nature photography competitions.

item.title: EIGHT baby capybaras are an 'overload of cuteness' at Isle of Man zoo
item.description: Owners of the Isle of Man zoo said they had their busiest ever October weekend with visitors desperate to see the pups.

item.title: Meet the snake clocking top speeds while rolling to safety
item.description: A team in Japan say they have worked out how the dwarf reed snake manages to roll to safety while maintaining control of where its going.

item.title: Blue Planet returning to take us deep beneath the waves
item.description: Blue Planet will be back on our screens in November for a third series, after its debut was broadcast 25 years ago. These kids joined Nina for an exclusive viewing and the chance to put their questions to one of its creators.

item.description: Scientists at Stanford |University in America have discovered that putting healthy coral next to bleached coral can help it fully recover in a matter of weeks

item.description: The leaves are starting to fall, there's a chill in the air and the evenings are drawing in - time to get a hot chocolate on the go, take our quiz and see just how much you know about the most colourful season of the year!

item.title: What is the Strait of Hormuz and why does it matter?
item.description: The war between US-Israel and Iran has reduced the amount of sea traffic that can get through this important passage.

item.title: BBC correspondent answers YOUR questions on US-Israel war with Iran
item.description: The US-Israel war with Iran in the Middle East is a big story in the news right now. It can be difficult to understand and keep up with what's happening, so BBC News correspondent Anna Foster is here to explain and to answer some of your questions.

item.title: Iran: 13-year-old Ava tells us what it's like to have family in the country
item.description: Emma-Louise caught up with 13-year-old Ava, who lives in the UK and has family in Iran, to find out what the last few days have been like.

item.title: What's happening in Iran?
item.description: The United States and Israel are continuing to carry out air strikes in Iran after war broke out on Saturday. Iran has responded by firing missiles at Israel and other countries in the region with links to the US, including Qatar, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Iran: Background to what's happening in the country
item.description: Iran's leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, has been killed in an attack by the US and Israel. Find out the background to Iran and its relationships with the United States and Israel.

item.title: How is the UK involved in the US-Israel war with Iran?
item.description: As the US-Israel war against Iran continues, we explain what the UK government and armed forces are doing in the region, and how some children in the UK and the Middle East are being affected.

item.title: US and Israel launch attacks on Iran
item.description: US President Donald Trump said in a video that their military has begun "major combat operations" with Israel against Iran.
